paragraphs: Look at who showed up, friend. Left-handed and right-handed archers. Gadites whose faces were like the faces of lions (1 Chronicles 12:8). Men from Issachar who "understood the times and knew what Israel should do" (1 Chronicles 12:32). Nobody was a copy of anybody else, and every one of them had a place in the crowd.

But they all came for one reason. The Zebulun men "with one purpose were devoted to David" (1 Chronicles 12:33), and the text says they came "in accordance with the word of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 12:23). They weren't just backing a winner. They were lining up behind what God had said. I can't get two bakers to agree on toppings, and here are tribes of men of one mind (1 Chronicles 12:38)!

So here's your big idea. You don't need to be the biggest, the loudest or the most polished to belong in what God is doing. Show up with what you've got, and stand with the ones standing on His word. I was a worn-out stamper in the back of a drawer, and I got pulled into a job too big for one stamper. The passage ends with "Indeed, there was joy in Israel" (1 Chronicles 12:40), and I think that's a good place to be.
